gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that the VIOFO A229 Plus's 60 fps front mode and its front HDR are either/or (BlackboxMyCar: enabling front HDR changes a 60 fps selection to 30 fps), so the '1440p 60 fps + HDR' line the rival pages print side by side is two separate modes.
standout_why: Compared against knowledgelib.io (cited), dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams (cited) and pcworld.com (cited); vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403, so I could not rule out that it already has this. knowledgelib already gives per-channel resolution for the A229 Plus 2CH (front 1440p 60 fps, rear 1440p 30 fps, IMX675 on both, HK4 needed) and the 70mai A810 Lite's drop to 24/25 fps with both cameras recording. DashCamTalk already has the A810 Lite's 'limited 24/25fps dual-channel recording' and the A810S at 30 fps. So rivals hold the 'both channels together' half of this angle. What they lack is the HDR-versus-60 fps footnote on the A229 Plus and a megapixels-per-channel column that puts '2K+2K', '4K+1080p' and '4K+2K' kits on one scale. The footnote rests on one named retailer guide, not the VIOFO manual, which I could not open.
decides: It confirms the A229 Plus 2CH as the pick but changes the reason. With HDR on (the night and plate setting) its front runs at 30 fps, so 60 fps is a daytime, HDR-off option, not an edge over the 4K kits at night. What still separates it is the rear camera: 2560×1440 on the same IMX675 sensor as the front, against 1920×1080 on the 70mai A810S and Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH. The under-$200 price holds only at third-party sellers: VIOFO's own US store lists the 2CH at $229.99 today. Our DDPAI N5 Pro (4K front + 1440p rear in the brief's record) would win 'most pixels on both channels under $200', but only if its price holds: the DDPAI store search today returned $259.00 for the N5 Pro listing, and I could not read the variants to reconcile that with the brief's $179.00 store / $157.52 link price.
